cards.explanation: The answer is from the heavens. Right at the top, the psalm says, "Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places." (Psalm 148:1) The psalm writer starts way up high and works his way down, friends. By verse 7 he gets to the ground: "Praise the LORD from the earth…" (Psalm 148:7)

The answer is angels, friends. The psalm says, "Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His heavenly hosts." (Psalm 148:2) They go first in the heavens. I once had an angel show up at my drawer, and I'm telling you, that's a choir member you want.

The answer is False. The writer isn't done with the sky yet. He says, "Praise Him, O highest heavens, and you waters above the skies." (Psalm 148:4) Even after all those shining stars, he keeps looking higher, friends.

The answer is that He commanded and they were created. The psalm says, "Let them praise the name of the LORD, for He gave the command and they were created." (Psalm 148:5) He spoke, and they were made, sun, moon and stars included. I can't even get my dough to rise when I ask nicely.

The answer is True, friends. The psalm says, "He established them forever and ever; He issued a decree that will never pass away." (Psalm 148:6) Forever and ever, and the decree never passes away. I can't even keep a batch of cookies around past Tuesday.

The answer is the earth. The psalm says, "Praise the LORD from the earth, all great sea creatures and ocean depths…" (Psalm 148:7) After all that sky, the writer brings the call down to ground level, friends. Well, ocean level, but you get it.
The answer is fulfilling His word. The psalm calls it "…powerful wind fulfilling His word…" (Psalm 148:8) The wind is doing what He said, friends. I wish my oven timer listened that well.

The answer is True, friends. The psalm says, "…fruit trees and all cedars…" (Psalm 148:9) The trees get a spot on the list, right along with the mountains and the hills. Fruit trees and all the cedars, together in one verse.

The answer is kings and rulers of the earth. The psalm says, "…kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth…" (Psalm 148:11) They lead off the people part of the list, friends. I think they might have been surprised to be in the same line as the sea creatures.
The answer is False. The writer doesn't split them up. He says, "…young men and maidens, old and young together." (Psalm 148:12) Old and young are called on together, friends.

The answer is that His name alone is exalted. The psalm says, "Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted…" (Psalm 148:13) Nobody else is lifted up like that, friends. His name alone.

The answer is a people near to Him. The psalm ends with "…of Israel, a people near to Him." (Psalm 148:14) After all that sky and sea, the writer ends on a people who are near, friends. I'd say that's a warm way to finish.
